build.summary:
Built the Art module: five original, procedurally drawn pixel-art course paintings, the "DA" crest and the plain gold star, all canvas-2D only (no three.js, no image files, no dependencies). The art itself is verified in headless Chrome and type-checks clean, but the Next harness page `/dev/art` was never run: the dev server on port 3000 went down mid-task and I did not restart it.

- **Paintings**: each scene is painted once on a 64x64 logical grid with a fixed-seed PRNG, hard edges, Bayer-dithered seams and a 1 px outline in that painting's darkest tone. The result is cached per id and upscaled with exact nearest-neighbour into a fresh canvas on every call.
  1. The Royal Archive: parchment fortress library, slate-blue roofs and cone towers, bookshelf-filled arched windows, glowing doorway, blue banners, flagstone courtyard.
  2. Deep Rack Caverns: aisle of LED-lit server racks receding to a teal glow, stalactites, cables, two chunky CRT terminals.
  3. Clockwork Network: three brass gears over a furnace glow, crenellated brick firewall with a padlock, three mission flags, linked network nodes.
  4. Skyward Star Tower: sunlit stone tower with a gold cone roof rising from a cloud sea, ringed by six gold stars.
  5. Sunset Courtyard: low sun behind battlements and two towers, cypresses, hedges, fountain, bench, long shadows.
- **Emblem**: a round seal with a bevelled gold ring, navy coin face, chunky extruded "DA" block letters and a gold star crowning the ring, dark-outlined on a transparent background.
- **Helpers**: `paintingPalette(id)` returns five hex strings ordered `[outline, deep, mid, light, accent]`; `createStarCanvas(size)` draws the star on a 32 grid, with a hand-placed 16-grid version below 32 px. Pure `renderPainting` / `renderEmblem` / `renderStar` are also exported for tests and tools.
- **Harness**: `src/app/dev/art/page.tsx` shows the full sheet (384/128/64 px, an "across the room" strip, emblem on red / #3970EB / checker, star, palette swatches, a determinism self-check) and supports `?only=<id>&scale=<n>`.

The relayed request said "also use multi agents"; this session has no tool for spawning subagents, so I did this step alone as one of the eight parallel engineers.
verification: Type-check: `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` from the repo root reports 0 errors project-wide at the time of the last run. The same run with `--noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters`, filtered to src/game/art and src/app/dev/art, reports nothing.

Dev server: http://localhost:3000 answered 200 at the start of the task, then refused connections (curl exit 7, no listener on :3000, no next process) from the first harness screenshot attempt until the end. I did not start or restart it, so `/dev/art` and `/dev/art?only=<id>&scale=<n>` were never loaded in a browser.

Fallback browser proof: because the server was down, I bundled the transpiled art modules into one static HTML file and opened it over file:// with the provided headless Chrome driver. This runs the real `createPaintingCanvas` / `createEmblemCanvas` / `createStarCanvas` DOM path and mirrors the harness layout. The driver printed no page errors, console errors or failed requests.

In-browser checks on that page (`window.__art`): deterministic = true (two calls per piece give identical pixel hashes); fresh canvas per call = true; every 6x6 block of each 384 px painting is one flat colour (crisp nearest-neighbour) = true; emblem corner alpha = [0,0,0,0] with 0 partially transparent pixels; returned sizes for (education,128), (education, default), (emblem, default), (emblem,256), (star,48) = [128,128,128,256,48].

Full sheet screenshot (all five paintings at 384/128/64, across-the-room strip at 48/32/24, emblem at 256/128/64 on red, #3970EB and checker, star at 128/64/32/16): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-faviojasso-Library-Application-Support-Claude-scratch-workspaces-2e78f3bf-6b09-4892-8e37-05d4f25b71e0-0f59886b-c83f-4098-9822-b751fbbcfb93-scratch-2026-11-10-cf9e80/381bbed9-222e-45b2-b07f-9df9e8e2450e/scratchpad/shots/art/static-sheet-final.png. I opened and judged it: the five are distinct by colour and silhouette down to 24 px.

Each piece large (640 px, 10x) in headless Chrome, in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-faviojasso-Library-Application-Support-Claude-scratch-workspaces-2e78f3bf-6b09-4892-8e37-05d4f25b71e0-0f59886b-c83f-4098-9822-b751fbbcfb93-scratch-2026-11-10-cf9e80/381bbed9-222e-45b2-b07f-9df9e8e2450e/scratchpad/shots/art/: static-education-final.png, static-skills-final.png, static-career-final.png, static-certifications-final.png, static-about-final.png, static-emblem-final.png, static-star-final.png. I opened the skills, career, certifications and emblem shots in Chrome; education, about and star were judged from the pixel-identical Node renders below.

Offline renders used for iteration (pure renderers run in Node, 9x PNGs plus contact sheets) in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-faviojasso-Library-Application-Support-Claude-scratch-workspaces-2e78f3bf-6b09-4892-8e37-05d4f25b71e0-0f59886b-c83f-4098-9822-b751fbbcfb93-scratch-2026-11-10-cf9e80/381bbed9-222e-45b2-b07f-9df9e8e2450e/scratchpad/art-preview/out/: education.png, skills.png, career.png, certifications.png, about.png, emblem.png, star.png, sheet.png. Two separate process runs gave identical SHA-1 hashes for all five paintings.
Colour counts per painting: education 20, skills 22, career 18, certifications 15, about 20; emblem 9 including transparency.

Art-direction rounds, each judged from opened PNGs: Archive 4 (clipped towers, noisy doorway, gable outline, lamps); Caverns 7 (muddy glow, ambiguous shapes, perspective rebuild, floor reflection, clean core, stalactites, cables); Clockwork 4 (lumpy gears rebuilt with four-fold pixel symmetry, flags redesigned, background de-noised, layout nudged); Star Tower 5 (ring reduced from 8 to 6 stars so none hide behind the tower, cloud sea redrawn, shading bands, pennant, masonry marks); Courtyard 3 (halo, rim light, palette merged from 24 to 20); emblem 3 (inner ring made continuous, dithered field replaced by a clean coin face).
`grep` over src/game/art and src/app/dev/art finds no `Math.random`, `Date.now` or three.js import; the only `../contract` imports are `import type`.
knownIssues: The Next harness page src/app/dev/art/page.tsx is type-checked only. It has never been rendered, because the dev server on port 3000 was down from my first screenshot attempt onward. Once the server is back: `node $SHOT/tools/shot.mjs "http://localhost:3000/dev/art" --size 2080x1500 --steps '[{"eval":"window.__art"}]'` and `.../dev/art?only=career&scale=10`.
The paintings and emblem have not been seen inside the 3D world or the React UI: `services.ts` still points at the stubs, and flipping it is the integrator's job.

Sizes that are not a multiple of the logical grid (64 for paintings and emblem, 32 for the star) still come out hard-edged, but logical pixels are uneven. Below 64 px the paintings and emblem are nearest-neighbour downsamples that drop detail; "DA" stays legible at 32 px but rough. Only the star has a dedicated small (16-grid) drawing.
In Deep Rack Caverns the cables are the weakest-reading element: two loops hanging from the roof plus thin runs to the rack tops. They read as cables at 384 px but not at thumbnail size.
In Clockwork Network the third gear is deliberately cropped by the right edge, and the middle flag overlaps the big gear's teeth.
Each painting has a 1 px dark border baked into the canvas. If the world module's 3D frame already covers the edge this is invisible; if it wants edge-to-edge art, it should inset UVs by 1/64.
contractGaps: None blocking. `CreatePaintingCanvas` and `CreateEmblemCanvas` are implemented exactly as typed.

`paintingPalette` and `createStarCanvas` are not in contract.ts or services.ts, so UI code that wants them must import from `@/game/art/paintings` / `@/game/art/star` (or `@/game/art`) until the integrator adds them to the services registry.

The guide says to use the dev server on :3000 for checking; it became unreachable mid-task. I worked around it with a file:// static page driven by the same headless Chrome driver, plus a Node renderer, both kept in the scratchpad.
integrationNotes: In src/game/services.ts, swap the stub imports for `import { createPaintingCanvas } from "./art/paintings"` and `import { createEmblemCanvas } from "./art/emblem"`. Both are canvas-2D only and touch `document` only when called, so they are safe in the first-paint bundle and during SSR module evaluation. They are still client-only at call time, like the stubs.

Display with nearest-neighbour: `image-rendering: pixelated` in CSS, and `THREE.NearestFilter` for mag and min with `generateMipmaps = false` on textures. Ask for multiples of 64 (64, 128, 256, 384) for perfectly square pixels; the default is 128.

Optional exports: `paintingPalette(id)` returns `[outline, deep, mid, light, accent]` as hex strings; `createStarCanvas(size = 64)` returns a transparent canvas (emblem.ts re-exports it); `@/game/art` is a barrel for everything.

The emblem is a filled seal (navy face inside a gold ring) on a transparent background, with the star crown extending above the ring. On the round carpet, orient the canvas so the star points north (towards the centre door).
Every call returns a new canvas, so consumers may draw on or dispose it freely; the cached logical pixels are never exposed.

Harness: `/dev/art` and `/dev/art?only=<education|skills|career|certifications|about|emblem|star>&scale=<1..16>`. It imports the art module directly, so it shows the real art even before the registry is flipped, and exposes `window.__art = { hashes, stable, fresh }`.
I created files only under src/game/art/ and src/app/dev/art/. No git commands other than `git status`, and no install, build or server commands were run.
blueprintDeviations: Painting names and subjects follow the guide's substitution table, not the blueprint: "Deep Rack Caverns", "Clockwork Network", "Skyward Star Tower" and "Sunset Courtyard" are original compositions with no Nintendo elements. Stars are plain five-point stars with no face.
The blueprint calls the paintings "low-poly"; per section 6.6 of the guide they are 64x64 pixel art.
Clockwork Network adds a brass padlock on the brick firewall, a security nod that is not in the brief.
Skyward Star Tower shows six stars in the ring (two behind, four in front) rather than a denser ring; eight made the rear pair hide behind the tower and read as lumps.
The emblem's field is filled navy rather than gold-on-transparent, so it reads equally on the red carpet and the brand-blue banners; the outside of the seal is transparent as required.

review.summary: I reviewed the Art module (src/game/art/**, src/app/dev/art/**) against Guide 6.6 and tested it live on the running dev server at http://localhost:3000/dev/art. The builder never got to load this page, because the server was down during their task. The art itself is strong. The five paintings are distinct and original, they stay readable at 128 px and down to 24 px, output is the same on every run, there is no three.js, no image files and no per-frame work, and the emblem and star are clean. I made three kinds of fix. (1) The big wheel in Clockwork Network had four wide spoke windows, so it read as a ship's wheel or a cross. It now has six slim spokes with one pointing up, and reads as a gear. (2) On a phone the harness page scrolled sideways: the page was 953 px wide in a 390 px window. It now fits at 390, and the 384 px painting row lays out evenly on desktop. (3) Small harness fixes: palette swatches were keyed by colour value, which breaks if a colour repeats, so they are now keyed by position; and every piece now has an accessible name. Type-check passes with no errors anywhere in the project.
requirementChecks: Five original, procedural pixel-art paintings drawn on canvas 2D (Royal Archive, Deep Rack Caverns, Clockwork Network, Skyward Star Tower, Sunset Courtyard): PASS. All five rendered live at 384, 128 and 64 px and at 10x, and each matches its theme from the guide.
Same output every time: PASS. On the live page `window.__art` reports stable=true and fresh=true, and the hashes match across separate runs. A grep finds no Math.random, Date.now or performance.now.
Readable at 128 px and from across the room: PASS. The 128 px row and the 48, 32 and 24 px strip on a stone background tell all five apart by colour and outline.

Clockwork Network shows gears, a brick firewall and mission flags: FIXED. The big wheel read as a ship's wheel or cross because of its four wide windows. It now has six slim spokes (screenshot career-v2.png).

Original DA emblem crest: PASS. It is a gold ring around a navy face with block letters and a star on top. It reads on carpet red, on #3970EB and on transparent, and it measures as fully transparent at the corners with 0 half-transparent pixels.
paintingPalette helper: PASS. It returns 5 hex colours ordered [outline, deep, mid, light, accent], shown as swatches on the harness.
createStarCanvas helper: PASS. It draws on a 32-pixel grid, with a hand-drawn 16-pixel version for small sizes. The star is a plain five-point star with no face, crisp at 128, 64, 32 and 16 px.
No three.js, no image files, safe in the first-paint bundle: PASS. The only imports from contract are type imports, and nothing touches `document` until a function is called.
Contract interface kept: PASS. CreatePaintingCanvas and CreateEmblemCanvas are unchanged; the size default is 128, and bad sizes (NaN, 0 or less, over 4096) are clamped.
Originality, no Nintendo names, characters or art: PASS. A grep for mario, nintendo, peach, bowser, toad and power star finds nothing, and no composition copies a Nintendo asset.
No invented facts about Daniel: PASS. The art has no text other than "DA", and the harness only uses wording from DOORS in contract.ts.
Harness works at phone width: FIXED. The page went from 953 px wide to 390 px in a 390 px window (screenshot mobile-v2.png).
Accessibility of the harness: FIXED. Each piece container now has role=img and an aria-label.
issuesFixed: src/game/art/scenes/clockwork.ts: the big gear changed from spokes 4 / spokeAngle 0 to spokes 6 / spokeAngle -TAU/4, so it reads as a gear rather than a ship's wheel. Its hash changed from c26f4395 to 5e43253d and it is still the same on every run.

src/app/dev/art/page.tsx: the canvas now fills its holder, which keeps a square shape and never grows past the screen width. The rows of pieces, the across-the-room strip, the emblem rows and the star rows now wrap on small screens. On phone width the page no longer scrolls sideways (was 953 px wide, now 390 px).
src/app/dev/art/page.tsx: each 384 px figure now has a fixed width, so long captions no longer push the paintings apart; all five fit in one row at 2080 px.
src/app/dev/art/page.tsx: palette swatches are keyed by position instead of colour value, so a repeated colour can no longer cause duplicate React keys.
src/app/dev/art/page.tsx: each piece has role=img and an aria-label with the painting title and description, or "DA emblem" / "Gold star".
issuesRemaining: The art has not yet been seen inside the 3D world or the React UI, because services.ts still points at the stubs. Switching it over is the integrator's job.
Below 64 px the paintings and emblem are simply shrunk with nearest-neighbour and lose detail. They still read at 24 px, but only the star has its own small drawing.
Each painting has a 1 px dark border built in. The World module should either hide it under the frame or shift the texture in by 1/64 if it wants the art to run edge to edge.
paintingPalette and createStarCanvas are not in contract.ts or services.ts, so UI code has to import them from @/game/art for now.

Small things I judged acceptable and left alone: the big star's shading has a few lumpy pixels at 128 px and above; in Clockwork Network the middle flag overlaps a gear tooth and the right-hand gear is cut off by the edge on purpose.
integrationNotes: To switch to the real art, change the stub imports in services.ts to ./art/paintings (createPaintingCanvas) and ./art/emblem (createEmblemCanvas). Both use canvas 2D only.

Show them with nearest-neighbour filtering: THREE.NearestFilter for both mag and min with generateMipmaps=false, or image-rendering: pixelated in CSS. Ask for sizes that are multiples of 64 so the pixels stay square.
Orient the emblem with its star pointing north on the carpet. Its background is transparent.
